category: 2026 DRC-Uganda-France BDBV Outbreak (Active — PHEIC; deadliest and largest ever recorded in DRC)
killed: 2,786 confirmed DRC / 2 confirmed Uganda = 2,788 confirmed total
injured: 3,006 surviving confirmed cases; 843 currently hospitalized in isolation (DRC); Uganda outbreak closed with 18 recoveries
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker / Al Jazeera — 27–28 August 2026
note: DRC: 5,794 confirmed cases across 60 of 151 health zones in 6 provinces as of 27 August (ECDC tracker, updated 28 August, +81 cases and +42 deaths day-on-day); 2,786 confirmed deaths; crude national CFR nearly 48% overall, but roughly 69% in Beni health zone (122 cases/87 deaths) and approximately 70% in North Kivu province more broadly. Two new health zones — Biena and Manguredjipa, both North Kivu — were added since the prior update. The outbreak has now surpassed the 2018-2020 Kivu epidemic's 3,317 cases to become the largest ever recorded in DRC. Africa CDC officials warned 22 August that true case counts could be 2-3x higher (10,000-15,000) given official detection may capture only 30-40% of infections, and that transmission may have begun as early as February 2026. Uganda: 20 confirmed cases (2 deaths, 18 recoveries) — declared over by its own Ministry of Health 28 July 2026 and confirmed over by WHO on 25 August after completing the 42-day monitoring period. France: 1 case, recovered and discharged 4 July, no secondary transmission. 155-160 confirmed cases among healthcare workers. UN Secretary-General António Guterres told the Security Council on 27 August that more than 40 healthcare workers had been killed, roughly 1 million people displaced in Ituri Province, and the response was only 48% funded, appealing for an additional $1.1 billion and warning of 'the virus of indifference.' DRC launched an Ervebo vaccination campaign for frontline workers under a compassionate-use framework on 27 August in Kisangani, covering 14 health zones in Tshopo, Bas-Uélé and Haut-Uélé — separate from the 20,000-dose Phase 3 Bundibugyo cross-protection trial, which had not yet launched as of 28 August.

category: West Africa Epidemic 2014–2016 (Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone)
note: Official confirmed + probable deaths. Excess mortality estimates 17,000–30,000 total. ~500 healthcare workers killed. Liberia: 4,809 dead; Sierra Leone: 3,956; Guinea: 2,545.

source: WHO / DRC MoH — End of Outbreak Declaration, 25 June 2020
note: 2nd-largest Ebola outbreak in history. CFR 66%. 168 healthcare workers infected, 41 killed. Sustained over 25 months in active conflict zone.
CFR 88% — highest ever recorded for Ebola. Primary amplification through reused syringes at Yambuku Mission Hospital. Isolated community; full case capture likely.
CFR 53%. Concurrent with Yambuku. Cotton factory and hospital workers primary cases. Led to identification of Sudan ebolavirus as distinct species.
CFR 79%. 315 total cases. Amplified through Kikwit General Hospital. Index case was forestry worker. High HCW toll (nurse family clusters).
CFR 53%. 425 total cases. Largest SUDV outbreak on record. Spread along trucking route Gulu-Masindi-Mbarara before containment.

category: Healthcare Worker Deaths — All Outbreaks Combined (1976–2026)
source: WHO Cumulative Health Worker Tracking; CDC
note: Largest single HCW toll: West Africa 2014 (~500 killed). Kivu 2018–2020: 41 killed. 2026 outbreak: 4 killed (as of May 2026). HCW deaths are central to response disruption and community trust breakdowns.

CFR 25% — lowest of any Ebola strain. 149 total cases. Identified new strain BDBV. Index case linked to dead chimpanzee. CFR difference vs EBOV (~60–90%) thought related to different receptor binding.

164 total cases; CFR 34%. No licensed SUDV vaccine available. Mubende District epicenter. Contained without licensed vaccine — contact tracing and ETU care alone. Exposed critical vaccine portfolio gap.
